selection.method: Source-only selection from current AWS-owned and independent Strands/AgentCore repositories after canonical Amazon depth-parity closure. No HorusTrace output from this cohort was used to select cases. Every target is pinned to an exact commit SHA and scanned at an application-level path.
selection.interpretation: Fresh unseen Amazon agentic holdout testing repository composition, helper/factory patterns, dynamic MCP catalogues, multi-agent delegation, Graph/Swarm, hooks, AgentCore memory/runtime and AWS tool authority.

cases.source_signal: ChatAgent creates a Strands Agent through an instance method using dynamically filtered repository tools, AgentCore Memory/session management and source-defined approval hooks for email/GitHub write operations. Runtime registry breadth may remain unresolved, but the agent, dynamic tool binding and enforcing hooks must not disappear.

One Strands agent combines file read/write with tools dynamically listed from two explicit stdio MCP clients (AWS documentation and pricing), including AWS credentials passed to one subprocess. Both MCP server identities/transports and dynamic catalogue binding should remain visible.

call_agent constructs Strands agents around runtime-configured Streamable HTTP or SSE MCP endpoints and binds list_tools_sync results. Endpoints are operator/runtime configured; remote MCP authority must remain explicit without inventing tool catalogues.

Main orchestrator composes a large list of specialist Strands agents directly as tools together with use_aws, file read/write, editor and shell. Delegated specialist authority and high-authority local/AWS tools should project into the orchestrator.

Customer-support supervisor builds a Strands Agent from a repository-composed tools list with AgentCore session/memory integration and specialist orchestration. Source-proven bound authority should survive factory/helper composition while runtime-only catalogue dimensions remain unresolved.

get_agent returns a Strands Agent whose tool list includes search/extraction tools and conditionally appends an SNS notification tool based on environment configuration. The agent and statically possible conditional authority should be retained without assuming SNS is always enabled.

An orchestrator binds a runtime MCP catalogue, a decorated weather tool that internally constructs another Strands Agent, plus http_request and shell. The fixed stdio MCP server, nested-agent source authority and high-authority vended tools should remain visible.

Production-style orchestrator constructs agents from database definitions, then selects Strands Swarm or Graph dynamically with runtime limits and a source-defined cancellation hook that cancels model/tool calls. Dynamic membership should stay unresolved but orchestration/control authority must remain represented.

TradingSwarm constructs full and fast GraphBuilder workflows from specialist agents returned by cross-file create_* factories, with parallel edges converging on a coordinator. Graph topology should be retained and member authority should be projected where source-resolvable.

AWSDevOpsAgentV2 builds a Strands Agent on an instance attribute from a large repository-local tool list spanning cost, security, IaC and AWS operations, with explicit safety/consent configuration. Class/factory construction must not hide the principal or its bound authority.
